newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - March 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - March 15.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
SEVEN KILLED, 13 INJURED IN PUNJAB BOMB BLAST
Seven people were killed and at least 13 injured in a bomb blast outside the Jalandhar railway station in Punjab. No militant outfit has claimed responsibility.
The Hindustan Times
EXTENSION OF CENTRAL RULE IN UTTAR PRADESH APPROVED

The statutory resolution extending president's rule in Uttar Pradesh for another six months from April 17 was passed by the lower house. Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) members opposed the resolution before walking out of the House in protest. Significantly, the BJP's allies, Shiv Sena and Samata party members, remained in the house when the resolution was put to vote.
The Economic Times
INDIAN ORGANIC TO HIVE OFF MADRAS PSF UNIT

Indian Organic Chemicals will hive off its two billion rupee polyester staple fibre (PSF) unit in Madras into a separate subsidiary. Indian Organic's PSF business has been incurring huge losses for the past few years and transferring it into a subsidiary would help strengthen the firm's organic chemicals business.
LIFE INSURANCE CORP PLANS UNIT-LINKED SCHEME

The Life Insurance Corporation (LIC) plans to introduce a Unit-Linked Life Insurance Scheme, where the premium component of an insurance policy would be remitted into a separate fund and invested in the capital market. Such a corpus would have the basic objective of a mutual fund, but would be managed internally. The investment risk would be borne by the policy-holder but he would not have to pay an additional amount.
Financial Express
FOREIGN INVESTOR HOLDINGS IN STATE BANK DOWN

Foreign institutional investor holdings in State Bank (SBI) shares were down to 16.52 percent due to profit-taking in the post-budget rally. Several other scrips, where the FII investment limit of 24 percent had already been reached, also witnessed profit-booking by foreign funds after domestic operators pumped up prices in post-budget euphoria. However, fresh FII buying in these scrips was hampered due to the delay in getting the changed position notified by the apex bank.
DISMAL CORPORATE RESULTS TO ERODE BULL-RUN GAINS

With the budget euphoria fading out, full-year corporate performance is likely to give a few shocks to the index. Going by the corporate performance in the first-half, an erosion in earnings is on the cards. The blind run on the bourses has ignored the dismal first-half corporate performance.
DISCREPANCIES PREVENT FRESH BUYING

The time-lag between the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) notification to bourses and custodians on the extent of foreign fund holdings in various scrips is hampering foreign institutional investor (FII) purchases. Foreign funds have been unable to buy shares in companies where FII holding is below the maximum 24 percent limit. There have been discrepancies in the past on net FII purchases and sales positions compiled by the RBI and the bourse regulator, custodial sources said.
TOP 100 WILL SEE EARNINGS GROW BY 25 PCT NEXT FISCAL YEAR

James Capel B&K revised its earnings growth projections for the top 100 Indian corporates from 19 percent to 25 percent for 1997/98 (April-March). Reduction in corporate tax announced in in the budget would upgrade the earnings growth of the top 100 companies. The Indian research-cum-broking arm of the HSBC group projected a near-zero growth in earnings for the top 100 companies for fiscal 1996/97. Collective earnings growth for 1995/96, according to James Capel, stood at 23 percent.
Business Standard
PUNJAB FARMERS SHUN WHEAT PROCUREMENT AGENCIES

The government's hopes of reversing the previous year's decline in wheat procurement may be hit by farmers' reluctance to accept the proposed minimum support price. The farm lobby has demanded a hike in procurement prices to bring them in line with international prices. Their stand intensified after the Punjab chief minister announced that the state government would advise wheat growers not to sell their produce to official procurement agencies at such low prices.
FOREIGN EXCHANGE RESERVES JUMP $600 MLN TO $20.6 BLN

The Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) foreign currency assets are estimated to have surged by $600 million in the previous seven days to touch $20.6 billion. The surge witnessed in the previous week was $200 million more than the $400 million mopped up by the RBI in the week after the budget. Bankers expected the figure to increase further on account of increased foreign institutional investor (FII) inflows as well as continuous RBI buying in the foreign exchange market.
BOMBAY BOURSE REMAINS VOLATILE IN POST-BUDGET SESSIONS

Post-budget trading on the Bombay bourse continues to be volatile. In the week after the budget, the sensitive index (Sensex) surged 469.82 points to close at 3944.61 on March 4. But by March 13, the Sensex rolled back to 3745.31, shedding about 200 points in the process. Marketmen, claiming the euphoria was intact, said the market could not sustain its over-bought position.
The Observer
FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS TO EXTEND PLEDGES FOR FOREIGN BANKS

Financial institutions (FIs) have agreed to extend a guarantee to foreign banks with a substantial stake in telecommunications projects. In lieu of their guarantee, the FIs would seek a modified form of corporate guarantees from the borrower companies. The assurance is significant in the light of a massive cash crunch being faced by Indian telecommunications companies.
The Asian Age
CONSOLIDATED ENERGY'S PLAN SENT FOR APPROVAL

Consolidated Energy Asia-Pacific's proposal to set up a 3,900-megawatt power project in Hirakud has been referred to the Central Electricity Authority (CEA) for its techno-economic clearance. The project, estimated to cost over 180 billion rupees, is expected to be financed by various multinational agencies, including some leading Indian financial institutions. Although project details are yet to be worked out, the Taiwan-based company said the project would be the largest power project in India promoted by any foreign company so far.
The Observer
NORMS FOR PRIVATE, FOREIGN ROLE IN INSURANCE SOON

The Insurance Regulatory Authority (IRA) is set to lay down rules governing private and foreign participation in the insurance sector within three months. Announcing this, the IRA chairman said amendments to insurance regulations were also in the offing once the Insurance Regulatory Authority Bill was passed by parliament.
